title: Hermes Discord so session orchestration

branch_policy.reason: Hermes and watchdog orchestration are experimental/development surfaces unless explicitly promoted.

user_story: A user opens a Hermes session in Discord and sends `so omp qt-bot fix blah using z-debug`. Hermes creates and registers the tmux-backed job, supervises it, consumes watchdog events, asks the requester for input by default, records feedback, and detects stale/dead sessions without blind sleep/capture polling.
hard_constraints: `so` is Discord/Hermes command language, not a z-harness CLI or local binary.
Do not require or expose user-provided tmux names such as `so-session`; Hermes generates internal session names and only shows them as diagnostics.
Do not use fixed `sleep N && tmux capture-pane ...` loops as orchestration. Captures must be event-driven: launch confirmation, watchdog alert, explicit status/log request, or bounded stale check.
Ask-first behavior is mandatory initially. Hermes sends no session input until the requester replies unless a future reviewed/promoted learned pattern exists.
No hardcoded initial replies for `/new`, handoff ingestion, `continue`, or similar prompts.
Pattern mining/review/promotion is a separate task after ask-first flow and fake e2e are working.
For Hermes-supervised `so` sessions, `job_id` is mandatory in watchdog routing; Hermes exports `HERMES_SO_JOB_ID=<job_id>` into the launched tmux session.
`next_step` is optional webhook metadata, not required routing data.
`execution_host`, `transport`, `ssh_target`, and `workdir` in the Hermes job record are authoritative for tmux/pid/capture/send-keys/attach/restart/abort operations.
Automated tests must use fake Discord and fake tmux/OMP; they must not contact real Discord, real OMP, real tmux, or real project repos.
No `REMOTE_VERIFY` tags unless an implementation task explicitly dogfoods `qt-bot` on its remote host.
